topics.title: Business Arithmetic
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: describe and calculate profit (includes all expenses incurred), loss, commission, interest, insurance and discount. (k, u)
express profit or loss as a percentage. (u)
solve simple interest problems. (k, s, v/a)

body.text: Profit is made when the selling price is more than everything spent to acquire and sell an item (the cost price, including any expenses like transport); a loss happens when the selling price is less. Profit = selling price - cost price (and expenses); loss = cost price (and expenses) - selling price.
A trader buys a bicycle for UGX 150 000, pays UGX 10 000 to transport it, and sells it for UGX 200 000. Total cost = 150 000 + 10 000 = 160 000. Profit = 200 000 - 160 000 = UGX 40 000.

Profit or loss is often expressed as a percentage of the cost price, so different sales can be compared fairly. Percentage profit = (profit ÷ cost price) x 100. For the bicycle: (40 000 ÷ 160 000) x 100 = 25%.

Commission is a payment (often a percentage of a sale) made to someone for arranging a deal; a discount is a reduction from the marked price, usually to encourage a sale. Simple interest is money earned or charged on a loan or savings, calculated only on the original amount (the principal), using I = PRT ÷ 100, where P is the principal, R is the rate per year (as a percentage), and T is the time in years.
Ashok invests UGX 500 000 at a simple interest rate of 8% per year for 3 years. Interest = (500 000 x 8 x 3) ÷ 100 = UGX 120 000, so after 3 years his savings total 500 000 + 120 000 = UGX 620 000.
